title: William Shakespeare: The Eternal Bard
description: Plays, places, and numbers—five steps through England's greatest playwright.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet,' where "Wherefore art thou Romeo?" means "why," not "where"?
questions.explanation: Juliet isn't looking for him; she's lamenting that he's a Montague. Bonus myth: the word "balcony" never appears in the play. Stage tradition added it.

questions.question: In which English town was Shakespeare born?
questions.explanation: He was baptized there on April 26, 1564. Tradition puts his birthday on April 23, the same date he died in 1616. Neat, though only the baptism is on record.

questions.question: After leaving Stratford-upon-Avon for London, Shakespeare wrote Hamlet—what line opens its famous soliloquy?
questions.answer: To be or not to be
acceptedAnswers: To be or not to be
to be or not to be
to be, or not to be
choices: Now is the winter of our discontent
questions.explanation: In the 1603 "bad quarto," it reads "To be, or not to be—ay, there's the point." The version everyone quotes arrived with the Second Quarto a year later.

questions.question: Hamlet's 'To be or not to be' likely premiered at which Bankside playhouse, built by Shakespeare's company in 1599?
questions.explanation: They built it from the timbers of their old playhouse, dismantled over Christmas 1598. In 1613 a stage cannon torched the thatch; one man's burning breeches were doused with ale.

questions.question: Beyond the Globe stage, Shakespeare wrote poetry too—how many sonnets appear in his 1609 collection?
questions.explanation: Publisher Thomas Thorpe dedicated them to a mysterious "Mr. W.H.," still unidentified. Sonnet 145 may pun on his wife, Anne Hathaway: "'I hate' from hate away she threw."

imageHint: A historic 1623 folio that preserved many of his plays for posterity
